topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the key learning objectives, and frames the clinical and biological scope of the course.

topics.label: Cellular and developmental foundations of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops as a failure of normal tissue differentiation and architecture driven by the accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes, alongside the experimental models used to study it.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and histological progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumor invasion and metastatic spread define malignancy, illustrated through gross pathology and histological stages of tumor progression.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature, clinical dangers, and mechanisms of mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how benign and malignant tumors are classified and named, the risks posed even by non-invasive growths, and the physical mechanisms by which tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Tumour incidence across tissues, populations, and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across human tissue types, demographic groups, and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and clinical modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, diagnostic methods, successes, and practical limitations of screening for precursor and early-stage cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with a review of the learning outcomes and instructions for upcoming practical sessions.
